source: I need to have a closer look at the gallery.
A-and, combined with the report I found in the gallery...
Can this be saying... King Hamlet's death... that he was... killed?
No. I have no proof of that. I should keep a close eye on Hamlet.
He'll lead me to the truth. I'm sure of it.
So Hamlet suspected his father was murdered even before he knew.
So Hamlet suspects his father was murdered after all.
This old shack is older than I am, but not by much.
This is where all of the plague victim's things were stored. Including my mother's.
I can see nails coming through from the other side. It won't budge for my weight.
I need someone stronger. Who might want to help?
This is the lazzaretto where my mother was held...
I'm not certain what that dock-shack is for. It's been locked up tight for as long as I can remember.
When the Book erased them, where did they go, I wonder?
Am I damned? Is this hell?
What kind of God could allow this to happen?
I hope you're at peace, father.
I've come here to pray before the Virgin ever since I was a girl. When I think of praying these days... nothing comes to mind.
The King's bedchamber is under even tighter watch than Gertrude's.
Even now, I'll have to wait for Claudius to invite me in again.
I've been in there before. But only when... well...
Only in worlds where the Queen's passed away.
I've been in there before, when Claudius held private council over Fortinbras's hiding out nearby.
But... I wonder if it's possible to find a way to explore that room on my own.
Only two people have ever been allowed inside, as far as I know: the Queen, when the two of them are 'together'...
And Bernardo, who comes to deliver private news to him from time to time.
Not even my father is permitted entry unless the circumstances are dire.
Hmm. Father locked his door. That's unlike him.
There are a lot of books here, but I see the bit of parchment I'm looking for.
'Uncommon circumstances?'
I wonder how much Hamlet suspects of his father's death.
... And to what extent a snake was really involved.
I cannot act without evidence. I must follow Hamlet, and see where his path leads him. ...For now.
It's clear that Claudius took great pains to cover up his crime. Such a sad, unfortunate man.
This shelf is cluttered with books, both old and new.
This is a perfect source of linen. Horatio can use this to make canvas.
Er... I'll use one of my older garments.
I now have everything Horatio needed. Just need to find a time with he and Brit are both free.
Gertrude mentioned she'd hid Brit's letters somewhere with 'unheard wishes'. A wishing well does make sense.
Let me see... ah!
There's a loose stone inside the well. And... here they are.
I'll bring these to Brit as soon as she's free.
Ah! There are some eggs here.
Don't even think about 'borrowing' from my food stores.
I promise you, you won't like the consequences.
(...Maybe later...)
Better collect them to give to Horatio.
This is a perfect source of charcoal. Better collect some to give Horatio.
How did my father find anything on a desk this messy?
Father, how do you find anything on a desk this messy?
Messy? What on earth do you mean? It's organized precisely the way I like it!
It's unclear how Father finds anything on a desk this messy.
Hmm—there's a note here.
A missing lute... I wonder if I could find it for him?
That's the late Queen Astrid, Hamlet's grandmother.
Come to think of it, I've often heard about King Alexander, but nothing about Queen Astrid. I wonder why?
How peculiar.
She looks so peaceful there.
Hard to imagine her dying the way she did.
What are you rummaging around over there for? You know those books are the oldest in the gallery, right? They're delicate.
Oh. I was only... looking for something new to read.
That's a book on pregnancy sickness.
Something you want to tell me?
Ah. No.
(I just grabbed the first book I saw...)
You're so strange.
It's an old bookshelf—but tucked away between these books, there's a bound set of notes...
...The notes bear the emblem of a noble Danish house. ...House Brockenhuus. Brit's family?
Why would Brit keep personal notes in the gallery...?
'... No longer shall we meet before three in the morning. The docks are too busy at any other hour.' The docks... Hmm.
It sounds like she's meeting someone late at night. But who? And why?
These are the letters from Fortinbras's emissary. Brit evidently hid them here.
This is where Brit hid her notes.
Another old, dusty bookshelf.
I could never have been the savior you wanted. Not really.
It's Hamlet's father, and his namesake, the late King Hamlet.
...Come to think of it, I noticed a blank space on the walls in the gallery...
...Sorry that I doubted you. I promise we'll stop Quince.
...I liked him enough when he was alive, now that he's dead I'm not sure what to make of him.
...Could the King's ghost really be haunting this castle?
I recognize her handwriting. This must be it.
Mother's diary...
Simona. She was trapped in time just like me.
She's been through this before. She must know the way out of it all. And-- and if this is right, she's still alive!
But where is she?
This is... incredible. If this is true... I've got to find Simona and speak to her.
Sounds like she's living in town nearby.
Still hard to believe, even now.
I still need to see if I can find Simona. She must know something more.
To think that Simona escaped Quince for so many years.
I wonder what she must have gone through, living all alone, unable to share what she'd been through with anyone.
It's my father's lockbox. He kept all his personal items in there.
It's my father's lockbox. He keeps his personal items in there.
Nothing but the key can open it, I presume.
...But it's unlockable now.
There are pages in here, scattered and frayed.
H-how could... this reads like... it's almost as if...
As if time were repeating for him, too.
Is this what Father was afraid I'd find? The mad rantings of a man in my exact predicament?
He mentions a strange cursed book—what he was searching for, his way out—perhaps if I can find it... there's still an escape.
No wonder Father didn't want the others to find out about this.
Everyone saw Hamlet as a strong king. No one ever thought him insane.
But if people believe that insanity runs in the family's bloodline...
Then that's cause to remove not just Hamlet, but Gertrude and Claudius from Elsinore.
It's empty. Nothing but... ashes.
I've often heard him open and close it in the evenings. I know he had something in here, but... I'm too late.
A-ha! And here is Irma's key to Gertrude's Chambers.
I already retrieved the key Irma hid here.
The Queen has a private hearth to toast her feet at night, of course. It vents through the center of the castle tower.
This massive fireplace... it's kept burning by the servants day and night. It's the true castle hearth, I suppose.
Hmmm. Locked.
What're yeh doin' here, my lady?
I dunnah how you got yerself a key, but the Queen's chambers are private!
(Evidently I must attempt this when he's gone.)
And now it isn't. Key, meet keyhole.
The key to this room is supposed to be hidden in the planter...
Who would have access to Gertrude's chambers?
I know Father will be... killed here.
If I can get inside somehow... I can be there when it happens.
Father has been killed here before.
Father was murdered here.
I wonder if it's possible to find a way to enter Queen Gertrude's room and understand what happened.
I suppose the Queen must want her privacy.
Forgive me, Lady Ophelia, but I cannot let you leave.
The King himself ordered that I disbar you.
And now His Majesty is dead.
T-the way you said that... Your face...!
Go right ahead, Lady Ophelia. My apologies.
I still know about your little gambling ring, Cygnus.
With all due respect, that ain't enough to overrule a member of the Royal Family's word.
(...This won't work. I need to find someone who has the power to help me regain access.)
Ah! I see. Perhaps I ought to tell the Guard Captain about your gambling ring, then?
What? Y-you... know about that?
Er... I'll let you through. Just please don't tell Bernardo about what you saw. He'll have all of us running laps for hours.
Especially not after yeh ratted us out to Bernardo. My thighs are still pudding. I can hardly stand!
Dunnah how you found out about our gambling, but... y'must be some kind of sorceress...
If I can learn about that, what other dirty secrets might I find if I spend long enough in the guard chambers?
...As I was sayin', go right on ahead, m'lady. The gates are open.
Ah. Yeh saw us, then. Hell. I knew our secret'd get out eventually...
Er, I'll let you through. Just please don't tell Bernardo about what you saw. He'll have all of us running laps for hours.
Why not? I'd like to go for a stroll.
Your father decreed to Guard Captain Bernardo that you were not to leave the castle grounds after... well... you and Hamlet.
And with all of us guards on thin ice lately, I'd hate to anger the Guard Captain.
At least, not before I recoup my losses tomorrow night!—Er, I've said too much.
(Hmm. Sounds like there's more to this situation.)
(I wonder if the other guards know more.)
(Maybe if I knew what they were getting up to in the evenings.)
The gate's locked. Cygnus must have stepped out. Hopefully he'll return shortly.
It's Gertrude's diary.
Ophelia, what are you doing?
That's private.
(Right. Can't have a look while she's here.)
I'm right here. Hoping to open her little diary?
Oh, don't worry, I've already read the whole thing, obviously. But you don't have that privilege.
Get out before I report you.
Oh, no. Gertrude...
This is the information Hamlet wanted. Let's see what he wants to do with it.
This... this information could really tear apart the court.
It's a letter. Hmm.
Is something troubling you?
What are these papers?
Nothing of consequence. Come away from them.
(Right. Can't have a look while he's here.)
T-this is...
Claudius must have hated his father far more than I realized.
Apologies, my lord. I was, er, trying to leave without waking you.
I wonder if there's something inside this vase...
